headline: gas has broken above September's peak, and this time next year rose with this winter
commentary: UK power spot is 168.25 £/MWh, up 3.5% since our update on 12 October and now more than double where it was a year ago. On 13 October it touched 173.79, the highest level in the three years shown here. The gas front month, November, is 217.12 p/therm, up 5.0% since 12 October and about 4.5% above September's peak. Market reporting this week points to European gas near four-year highs, Europe needing around 9% more LNG this winter to support tighter storage, and French power heading for its highest weekly price since December 2022 as demand rises and gas-fired generation costs climb. The UK imports power from France, so that pressure reaches us too. This time the rise reached next year as well as this winter: November to January are up 5.0 to 5.8%, Q1 27 6.2% and Summer 27 7.9%. When the whole curve lifts like this, the market is pricing risk into next year too, so waiting for this winter to pass does not avoid it. A 12-month contract starting in November is about 0.8 p/kWh higher on a wholesale-equivalent basis than on 12 October. A 24-month is up around 0.7 p/kWh and still sits around 17% below the 12-month, so term still buys a lower average price. Waiting has now cost money in all three updates since late September. Day-ahead prices this week ran from £86.89/MWh to £153.37, and the floor is rising: the cheapest hour for 17 October is £114.51, the swing and the level a fixed price takes off the table.

gas.note: NBP front month Nov 26 is 217.12 p/therm, up 5.0% on its 12 Oct print of 206.75 and about 4.5% above September's peak, a new high for this run. The rest of this winter: Dec 26 220.86, Jan 27 222.52, Q1 27 218.00. Feb 27 214.32 is an early-morning trade, before most of today's rise, and March had no print. This time the back of the curve rose as much as the front, or more: November to January up 5.0 to 5.8%, Q1 27 +6.2%, Summer 27 162.91 (+7.9%). So the step down from this winter narrowed slightly: Q1 27 to Summer 27 is a 25.3% discount, from 26.5% on 12 Oct. Apr 27 (181.53) and Q4 27 (156.00) are shown for the first time. A rise across the whole curve means a longer contract does not dodge the increase, but it still blends this winter down with cheaper summers.
